newsitem.title: UK: Lord Gladwyn, British architect of UN charter, dies.
newsitem.headline: Lord Gladwyn, British architect of UN charter, dies.

text.p: Lord Gladwyn, a former permanent British representative at the United Nations, died on Thursday, aged 96, British officials said on Friday.

Born Hubert Miles Gladwyn Jebb, he played a key role in drafting the United Nations Charter and was acting secretary-general of the world body in 1946 until the appointment of the Norwegian Trygve Lie.
Jebb went to the exclusive Eton boys school before obtaining an honours degree in history at Magdalen College, Oxford.
He entered the British diplomatic service in 1924 and towards the end of World War Two was in charge of a section of the Foreign Office known as the reconstruction department.

It was set up to work out Britain's foreign policies after the war and he became engaged in drafting blueprints for the creation of the United Nations and other postwar international groups including the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).
The first draft of the U.N. constitution was prepared under his direction. As acting secretary-general, he organised the first U.N. General Assembly meeting, which took place in London in 1946.
He served as ambassador to Paris from 1954 until his retirement in 1960, when was made an hereditary peer.
Lord Gladwyn is survived by one son and two daughters. His wife Cynthia died in 1990.
